items.title: Will New VC Funding Rules Cause Valuation Inflation? Expert Debate | Point Break
items.summary:
The Indian government has revised its ₹10,000 crore Fund of Funds for startups, allowing venture funds faster access to capital. By enabling funds to draw down money earlier in their lifecycle, the government aims to fix the chronic "speed mismatch" between government disbursements and the aggressive pace of venture investing. But while faster capital is a welcome signal, investors remain deeply divided: Is the bottleneck actually a shortage of capital, or does India simply lack a pipeline of venture-ready deep tech companies?

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with two of India’s most seasoned deep tech investors, Manish Singhal (Founding Partner, Pi Ventures) and Anil Joshi (Founder & Managing Partner, Unicorn India Ventures), to break down whether faster money fixes the structural gaps in Indian R&D, how to distinguish between a research project and an investable startup, and why deep tech is a 10-year marathon that money alone cannot solve.

Does India have enough investable deep tech startups to absorb this capital, or are we just funding the same limited pipeline more quickly?
